OhQP: https://www.ohqp.org/index.php/rules/ plus /official-list-of-mults-for-ohio-stations/ and /official-list-of-mults-for-non-ohio-stations/. _provenance.txqp_county_codes: ⚠️ THE SPONSOR'S PROSE AND THE SPONSOR'S LIST DISAGREE, AND THE LIST WINS. txqp.net/?page_id=23 says "Log submissions must use the approved four-letter county abbreviation for the exchange." The official list on ?page_id=90 has 254 entries, of which TWO ARE THREE LETTERS: BEE (Bee) and LEE (Lee). A domain or validator written to the prose (len == 4) rejects two real Texas counties, and a Texas mobile operating in either one produces an unsubmittable log for every QSO made from it. The domain below is the sponsor's 254 codes verbatim. Do not normalise, pad or "fix" BEE and LEE, and do not generate codes from county names — the scheme is irregular (Brazoria=BZIA, Brazos=BZOS, Cameron=CMRN, Collin=COLN, Collingsworth=COLW, Comal=COML, Comanche=COMA, Dallam=DALM, Dallas=DALS).
_provenance.qso_party_county_adif: Every county domain below exports under NO standard ADIF column in either direction (adif rcvd and sent are both ""), and that is a finding, not an omission. MY_CNTY and CNTY both exist in ADIF 3.1.7 (https://adif.org/317/ADIF_317.htm, read 2026-09-09) — but they are Enumerations in the Secondary Administrative Subdivision format, which the spec's own table gives as <Two-letter state abbr.> COMMA <county name>, example "MA,Middlesex → Massachusetts state, Middlesex county". A contest abbreviation (FRAN, BEE) is not a legal value of that field, so writing one into <CNTY> would emit malformed ADIF that a reimport cannot resolve. ADIF's own answer for this case is the one taken here: SRX_STRING/STX_STRING, "use Cabrillo format to convey contest information for which ADIF fields are not specified", plus the private carrier (spec §3.5). A later batch may map a code to the ADIF form deliberately (the domain carries the county NAME as its label and the ruleset knows the state); guessing it here would ship an invented value into other people's logbooks. cqp_states is the one domain that DOES declare STATE/MY_STATE: its 63 codes are Primary Administrative Subdivision codes and nothing else. oh_mults does not, because the sponsor's own list ends with DX, which is not a subdivision code.
_provenance.qso_party_score_omissions: ⚠️ WHAT THE SCORE THESE RULESETS COMPUTE LEAVES OUT, and it is deliberate. TNQP and TXQP both award bonus points COMPUTED FROM THE LOG, and TNQP a multiplier gated on a per-county QSO count: TNQP — "All entrants may claim 100 bonus points for each QSO (one per band/mode) with TCG headquarters station K4TCG", "Tennessee mobile & rover operators may claim 500 bonus points for each Tennessee county from which they complete at least 10 QSOs. All bonus points are added after the geographic multiplier", and "Tennessee mobiles and rovers may claim one multiplier for any Tennessee county from which they complete at least 10 QSOs if they do not earn a multiplier for that county otherwise"; TXQP — 500 points per Texas mobile worked in each five different counties and 1000 points per county a Texas mobile covers with at least five QSOs. PostMultiplier::Bonuses is a menu the operator TICKS and MultiplierRule cannot express a count-thresholded, sent-side, otherwise-not-earned multiplier, so NEITHER TERM IS IN THE TOTAL. What ships is exchange, dupe, QSO points and geographic multipliers — which is what makes a log SUBMITTABLE, and a submittable log with an honestly incomplete score is recoverable where an unsubmittable one is not. Both rulesets carry score_note_key so the omission reaches the operator's screen rather than living here.
_provenance.qso_party_ambiguities: ⚠️ FOUR THINGS THE SPONSORS LEAVE UNDEFINED. They are quoted, not resolved: a wrong guess baked into a ruleset is invisible, and an operator can ask the sponsor. (1) TNQP's DX sent form has NO published form. The exchange says "…or DXCC entity" and the multiplier section says "DXCC entities (see ARRL DXCC list)"; the sponsor never states whether a DX station sends the entity name, the ARRL DXCC prefix, its own callsign prefix, or the literal DX. TXQP answers the identical question for itself and TNQP does not. Ask tnqsoparty@gmail.com. (2) TXQP's Texas Mobiles bonus paragraph is GARBLED on the sponsor's own page, verbatim: "Texas Mobiles—Add one thousand (1000) points to your FINAL SCORE per every county covered with at least five non-duplicate Add five hundred (500) bonus points to your FINAL SCORE for each Texas mobile worked in five (5) different counties regardless of band or mode." The sentence breaks after "at least five non-duplicate" and the non-Texas paragraph is pasted over the remainder. The intended word is almost certainly "QSOs" — which is a guess, so the term is omitted rather than completed. (3) TXQP publishes NO state / province / country abbreviation list, and "maritime region" is undefined as a sent value. (4) TNQP likewise publishes no state / province abbreviation list: its PDF states the UNIVERSE ("U.S. states (49 max/band – do not count Tennessee as a state, District of Columbia counts as Maryland)", "Canadian provinces/territories (13 max/band: British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland & Labrador, Yukon, NWT and Nunavut)") and no abbreviation table. Consequence for (1), (3) and (4): TNQP's and TXQP's non-in-state QTH arm is Text, not an Enum. A domain built from another sponsor's list would attribute one sponsor's abbreviations to another; a domain built from a convention would refuse a legal value the sponsor never constrained. The county arm — the multiplier that matters and the one every sponsor DOES publish — stays closed.
_provenance.qso_party_roles: OhQP is THREE roles because ohqp.org publishes three sending behaviours with a domain for each: "Ohio stations send RST and their Ohio county. … Non Ohio W/VE stations (including KH6/KL7) send RST and their state or province. … DX stations outside of W/VE send RST and \"DX\"." The w_ve role's my_location_in list is the sponsor's own 62-code list minus DX, so it INCLUDES AK and HI — the sponsor puts KH6/KL7 in the W/VE role explicitly, and a list built from the CONUS states would ship a KL7 entrant the DX role and the wrong exchange. CQP is two: the sponsor gives one non-California form covering state, province and DX. TNQP and TXQP are two rather than three: TXQP states a third sending behaviour ("DX stations should send the primary prefix assigned to their country") and TNQP states none, but neither publishes a domain for either non-in-state form, so a third role would differ from the second in nothing this build can express. Both non-in-state roles are the trailing `always` catch-all ContestSession::role falls through to.
_provenance.qso_party_dupe: Every one of the four keys on call + band + mode class + the received QTH + the SENT QTH, from each sponsor's own mobile rule. OhQP: "Stations may be worked once per mode on each band" + "Mobile stations that change geographic area (counties for Ohio stations, state or province for others) may be contacted again for QSO points and multiplier credit" + the 500-foot rule. CQP: "Stations may be worked once on CW and once on Phone on each of the 6 bands (maximum of 12 QSOs with any one station)" + "California Mobile stations which change counties or states are considered to be new stations and may be contacted again for point and multiplier credit"; note also "State-line operations are not allowed." TNQP: "Fixed Stations may be worked once per band/mode" + "Mobiles and Rovers may be worked again if they change counties". TXQP: "Stations may be worked only once per band per mode for QSO count. Texas mobiles may be worked only once per band per mode from each county for QSO count" + "For duping purposes, all digital sub modes are considered to be the same mode (Digital)."
_provenance.qso_party_points: TNQP "3 points per QSO regardless of mode" → PH/CW/DIG all 3. TXQP "Count two (2) points per phone QSO … Count three (3) points per CW and other digital mode QSOs" → 2/3/3. CQP 3 both modes, and the year matters: "Each complete non-duplicate Phone contact is worth 3 points. NEW IN 2026" — CQP raised Phone from 2 to 3 for 2026, so this table is wrong for 2025 and right for 2026. OhQP 1 phone / 2 CW. ⚠️ OhQP and CQP score DIG as 0 because neither sponsor runs a digital mode — OhQP "CW and SSB on 160, 80, 40, 20, 15, and 10 meters", CQP CW and Phone only. Zero is the honest value for a mode the sponsor does not run; it is not a missing number.
_provenance.qso_party_multiplier_scope: Each scope is the sponsor's own sentence. OhQP PER MODE: "MULTIPLIERS – Multipliers are counted once per mode, i.e. working the same multiplier on both CW and SSB counts as two multipliers." CQP PER LOG: "The final score is the total number of QSO Points multiplied by the total number of scored multipliers (58 maximum)." TXQP PER LOG: "Multipliers are counted once for the QSO Party. For example, if you work NC on SSB and on CW that counts as one multiplier." TNQP PER BAND: "Multipliers accumulate on a per band basis." ⚠️ For TNQP and TXQP the IN-STATE role's multiplier rule counts the whole QTH value rather than a named domain, because that role's universe is counties AND states AND provinces AND DXCC entities and only the county half has a published domain; the codes do not collide (4 letters vs 2), so one distinct-value bucket is the same count the sponsor describes. ⚠️ The DxccEntity rules on those two roles carried an EMPTY `excluding` list through batches 8 and 9 because nothing in the build could resolve an entity, so the rule counted nothing whatever it excluded. Batch 10 installs a country file (CQ WW needs one), which makes those two rules LIVE — so the sponsors' own exclusions are now written out: TNQP "DXCC entities (see ARRL DXCC list – less USA, Canada, Alaska & Hawaii — Do not count USA nor Canada as countries; Alaska & Hawaii count as states only)" and TXQP "DXCC countries excluding USA, Canada, Alaska and Hawaii". The four strings are cty.dat's own entity spellings (United States / Canada / Alaska / Hawaii), which is what `excluding` compares against; src-tauri's `the_vendored_country_file_places_the_calls_the_cq_contests_score_by` pins the spellings so a refreshed country file that renamed one goes red instead of quietly counting a multiplier the sponsor excludes.
_provenance.qso_party_windows: OhQP "occurs on the fourth Saturday of August. The contest period extends from 1200 EDT [noon] to 2400 EDT [midnight] (1600Z Saturday until 0400Z Sunday)" → month 8, 4th full weekend, 1600Z, 12 h (in August the 4th full-weekend Saturday and the 4th Saturday are always the same day). CQP 1600 UTC 3 Oct 2026 – 2200 UTC 4 Oct 2026 → month 10, 1st full weekend, 1600Z, 30 h. TXQP "SCHEDULED TO OCCUR ANNUALLY ON THE THIRD WEEKEND (SATURDAY AND SUNDAY) IN SEPTEMBER. Operating times are from 1400Z on SATURDAY to 0200Z on SUNDAY and from 1400Z to 2000Z on SUNDAY" → month 9, 3rd full weekend, 1400Z, 30 h. ⚠️ TXQP's period has a BREAK (0200Z–1400Z Sunday) that WindowRule cannot express, so the window here is the outer envelope; it is used for countdown and session bounds, never to refuse a contact. ⚠️ TNQP publishes ONLY the 2026 instants — "CONTEST PERIOD 1700z Sunday, September 6 until 0300z Monday, September 7, 2026" — and NO annual rule. The parameters below (month 9, 1st full weekend, start_hour_utc 41, 10 h) reproduce those instants exactly by reading them as the SUNDAY of the first full September weekend; that reading is this build's, not the sponsor's, and must be re-read before the 2027 event. start_hour_utc is hours from 0000Z on the anchor Saturday, which is why a Sunday start is 41 rather than 17.
_provenance.qso_party_cabrillo: ⚠️ TWO REGISTRIES, NOT ONE — AND FOR THREE OF THESE SIX CONTESTS THEY DISAGREE. Verified 2026-09-09. The contest_id below is an ADIF value and is written as the ADIF CONTEST_ID tag: all six are verbatim entries of the ADIF 3.1.7 Contest_ID enumeration (https://adif.org/317/ADIF_317.htm §III.B.5, fetched and searched in full 2026-09-09), each paired there with this contest's own name — ARRL-FIELD-DAY "ARRL Field Day", WFD "Winter Field Day (2017 and later)", TN-QSO-PARTY "Tennessee QSO Party", OH-QSO-PARTY "Ohio QSO Party", CA-QSO-PARTY "California QSO Party", TX-QSO-PARTY "Texas QSO Party" — and ADIF's CONTEST_ID row reads "QSO Contest Identifier — use enumeration values for interoperability". These six values are therefore RIGHT and must not be changed. Batch 8 recorded four of them as unverified guesses "following the WWROF contest-name convention"; that convention does not exist, but the strings coincide exactly with the ADIF enumeration, so what was wrong was the reasoning and the SECOND use they were put to — not the strings. THE TWO REGISTRIES ARE INDEPENDENT: a token verified in one says NOTHING about the other. ADIF's enumeration and the WA7BNM master list were compiled separately, by different people, from different sources, and they disagree for three of these six contests — so each of a contest's two tokens has to be checked against its own source, and a batch that confirms one has not confirmed the other. That is precisely the mistake this entry replaces. THE CABRILLO CONTEST: TOKEN IS A DIFFERENT NAMESPACE, and for three of these six it is a different string. The mapping lives in contest::cabrillo::cabrillo_contest_token and is applied at the last step before the header (FieldDayLog::cabrillo); it must never run backwards, because ARRL-FD, MRRC-OHQP and TXQP are NOT ADIF enumeration values (zero hits each in ADIF 3.1.7; positive control: ARRL-SS-CW and CQ-WW-CW both hit) and one of them in CONTEST_ID is an unresolvable token in somebody else's logbook. There is no authoritative Cabrillo list: the V3 header specification (https://wwrof.org/cabrillo/cabrillo-v3-header/, "Last update: 5 June 2025", read 2026-09-09) states that "Contest text values are not an official part of the specification. Contest sponsors may define their own contest values", and its own 31-name example list contains no Field Day and no state QSO party. It links the WA7BNM Contest Calendar "Master List of Cabrillo Names" (https://www.contestcalendar.com/cabnames.php, Revision Date February 23, 2026, read 2026-09-09) as the extension of that list; the master list states its names "were determined to be the official Cabrillo name for a contest from the contest sponsor's web site or an e-mail exchange with the contest manager", and it is the authority for five of the six. Its state-party names are IRREGULAR — 7QP, COQP, FCG-FQP, IAQP, KYQP, MRRC-OHQP, NEQP, NJQP, SDQSOP, TXQP, WIQP, WVQP sit alongside the XX-QSO-PARTY forms — so no Cabrillo token here could have been inferred from a shape. PER CONTEST. WFD is the ONLY sponsor-published token of the six and is the same string in both registries: the WFDA rules (https://winterfieldday.org/sop.php, body served from /queries/query_rules.php, read 2026-09-09) print a complete "Cabrillo Formatting Example" header carrying the literal line "CONTEST: WFD", though the same document says the header is largely ignored. ARRL Field Day is ARRL-FD to Cabrillo (master list id 57); ARRL publishes no token of its own and runs no Field Day robot — the 2026 Field Day Rules PDF §8.6 says "ARRL does not use the logs" and §8.7 accepts Cabrillo only in lieu of the dupe sheet, and Field Day is absent from the 15 contests at https://contest-log-submission.arrl.org/ (read 2026-09-09) — so ARRL-FD is for INTEROPERABILITY with everything downstream of Nexus (other people's log analysers, contest-club aggregators, a re-import), not to avoid a rejection. Ohio is MRRC-OHQP to Cabrillo (id 100), named for the Mad River Radio Club and not a form anyone would guess; OhQP cannot reject either value because https://www.ohqp.org/index.php/cabrillo-information/ (read 2026-09-09) says "OhQP does NOT use Cabrillo header info as it has been found over the years to be incorrect" and collects call, location, category and club on the upload page instead. Texas is TXQP to Cabrillo (id 133) and carries the only real forward risk of the three: the sponsor's rules (https://www.txqp.net/?page_id=23) require online submission at https://txqp.contesting.com/, which as of 2026-09-09 serves only "Future home of the Texas QSO Party log handling web site." That robot will be built by the author of the master list — the sibling TNQP robot's footer reads "Site by WA7BNM/N5KO/K5TR, sponsored by World Wide Radio Operators Foundation" — so TXQP is the token it is most likely to know. Tennessee and California are TN-QSO-PARTY and CA-QSO-PARTY in BOTH registries (ids 115 and 140) and are unchanged; neither sponsor publishes a token. TNQP is the one sponsor that says the header IS parsed ("The header information is used by the processing software and must be complete and accurate", Tennessee QSO Party 2026 Rules PDF, LOGS section), but the fields it enumerates are entry class, personal information, call sign, station location and e-mail — not CONTEST — so whether its robot validates the token is UNKNOWN. CQP publishes only QSO-line syntax, as two images (cabrillo-01.jpg/cabrillo-02.jpg on https://cqp.org/logsubmit-main.html), and its robot form (http://robot.cqp.org/cqp/logsubmit-form.html) collects callsign, e-mail, class and club. ⚠️ DO NOT shorten the California token to "CQP": on the master list CQP is the COLLEGIATE QSO Party (id 122), a different contest — and Nexus's own internal event key for California is cqp, which is exactly what makes the shortening look natural. UNESTABLISHED for all six: no sponsor documents what its robot does with an unrecognised CONTEST: value, so the failure mode a wrong token produces is still unknown; treat "unknown, assume rejection" as the safe reading.
_provenance.qso_party_bands: TNQP and TXQP both exclude bands — TNQP "All amateur bands are valid, with the exception of 60, 30, 17 and 12 meters", TXQP "Operation on all Amateur bands is permitted, except on 60 meters, 30 meters, 17 meters and 12 meters" — and OhQP restricts to 160/80/40/20/15/10. A ruleset has `banned_modes` and no band field, so none of this is expressed; it is advisory data a later batch can carry. No score or dupe depends on it.

_provenance.sections: ⚠️ THE TOP-LEVEL sections ARRAY IS 85, NOT THE 83 THIS FILE CARRIED UNTIL 2026-09-09, and the correction is a shipped-defect fix rather than a data refresh: operators in five current sections could not select their own section at all, and three retired codes were offered instead. SOURCE: two ARRL-published lists, both read 2026-09-09 and identical in content — https://www.arrl.org/section-abbreviations (ARRL's own section table, US call-sign areas 1–0 plus a Canadian block) and https://www.arrl.org/files/file/Field-Day/Generic/ARRL-RAC%20Section%20List.pdf (the generic Field Day section package, footer "Revised 2025"). Both state 71 US + 14 RAC = 85, which is also the count in contestmultipliers.php?a=wve's own sentence "These are the names of the 85 W/VE sections used in ARRL contests" that batch 9 read for ss_sections. THE THREE RETIREMENTS, IN THE SPONSOR'S OWN WORDS: the Field Day PDF prints "Golden Horseshoe GH (formerly GTA)" and "Territories TER (formerly NT)" — two RENAMES, published as such, which is why a stored GTA or NT is migrated to its successor without asking anybody. MAR (Maritime) is different, and the difference is the whole migration question: it appears on NEITHER list, and NB / NS / PE appear on both as three separate entries, because the section SPLIT. ARRL publishes no MAR alias and there is nothing to infer one from — a Maritime operator is in exactly one of three provinces and this file cannot know which. So MAR is NOT auto-mapped: fd_rules::retired_section reports it as a split with three successors, the operator is asked, and until they answer the session is refused by name rather than transmitting a guessed section for a whole contest. ORDERING: the RAC block follows the sponsor's own Canadian order (NL NB NS PE QC ONE ONN ONS GH MB SK AB BC TER); GH sits where GTA sat and TER where NT sat, so the two renames move no other section's board position. ⚠️ parse_spec pins the count at 85 and the shipped app enforces the same floor, so this array cannot be moved by a data push alone — a rules file with a different count is refused by every build that predates the change. tests/arrl_sections.rs transcribes the sponsor's 85 independently and holds this array equal to ss_sections, so the two lists in this file can no longer disagree.
_provenance.sweepstakes: ARRL November Sweepstakes ships as TWO rulesets, arrlss_cw and arrlss_ssb, written from https://contests.arrl.org/ContestRules/SS-Rules.pdf, Version 2.1, all 10 pages extracted and read 2026-09-09. TWO RULESETS AND NOT ONE MODE-SPLIT ROW: the sponsor runs them as separate contests on separate weekends ("CW: First full weekend in November / Phone: Third full weekend in November"; §2.4 "Use only CW during the CW weekend and Phone during the Phone weekend"), with separate certificates, separate Clean Sweep mugs and separate CONTEST tokens — and a WindowRule holds one weekend, so one row could not carry both dates whatever the token did. EXCHANGE (§4, verbatim): "4.1 Serial Number - a consecutive contact number starting with 1; 4.2 Precedence “Q” for Single Operator, QRP / “A” for Single Operator, Low Power / “B” for Single Operator, High Power / “U” for Single Operator Unlimited, High Power, Single Operator Unlimited, Low Power and Single Operator Unlimited, QRP / “M” for Multioperator, High Power or Multioperator, Low Power / “S” for School Club; 4.3 Your call sign (the call sign must be included during the exchange); 4.4 Check — 4.4.1 The last two digits of the year the operator or the station was first licensed. 4.4.2 The same Check must be sent throughout the contest; 4.5 Section – send and log the abbreviations in the ARRL Contest Multipliers List." ⚠️ The narrative on p.2 says "The following SIX pieces of information must be sent" and then enumerates FIVE, the same five §4.1–§4.5 lists; five ship and the count is a sponsor slip. "It is highly recommended that you send the information in this order" — RECOMMENDED, not mandatory, so the send order below is the sponsor's and a parser must not require it. SCORING (§5): "5.1 QSO points: Each contact counts for two (2) points. 5.2 Multipliers: ARRL/RAC Sections plus Northern Territories. 5.3 Final score equals the total QSO points times the total multipliers contacted." Two points is written here as points_by_mode_class PH/CW/DIG all 2 rather than a new flat-points model, because the sponsor's rule carries no mode qualification and widening the file's scoring vocabulary would strand every shipped build's rules updates on its bundled seed (§8d). DUPE (§2.2): "Each station may be contacted only once, regardless of band." — by_call true, by_band FALSE, by_mode_class FALSE. SECTIONS: the domain is ss_sections, 85 codes parsed off https://contests.arrl.org/contestmultipliers.php?a=wve (read 2026-09-09), which states "These are the names of the 85 W/VE sections used in ARRL contests, along with their standard abbreviations." ⚠️ THE TERRITORIES ABBREVIATION IS TER, NOT NT. §5.2's phrase "plus Northern Territories" is prose, not an abbreviation; NT does not appear anywhere in the sponsor's list. ⚠️ ss_sections IS NOT fd_sections, and the difference is a live defect in the OTHER list, recorded here and deliberately not fixed in this batch: the top-level sections array this file has always carried holds 83 codes from an older ARRL era — MAR (Maritime, since split into NB/NS/PE), GTA (since renamed GH, Ontario Golden Horseshoe) and NT (since TER). Correcting it moves Field Day's section domain, the TypeScript section mirror and the §8(a) goldens, which is its own change. Sweepstakes therefore declares its own domain from the sponsor's current list. CABRILLO: the tokens are ARRL-SS-CW and ARRL-SS-SSB and BOTH REGISTRIES AGREE for once — ADIF 3.1.7's CONTEST_ID enumeration (https://adif.org/317/ADIF_317.htm, "updated 2026-03-22", read 2026-09-09) lists ARRL-SS-CW = "ARRL November Sweepstakes (CW)" and ARRL-SS-SSB = "ARRL November Sweepstakes (Phone)" and carries no unsplit ARRL-SS; the WA7BNM master list the Cabrillo V3 specification points at (https://www.contestcalendar.com/cabnames.php, Revision Date February 23, 2026, read 2026-09-09) carries the same two strings at ids 177 and 178; and ARRL's OWN page https://www.arrl.org/cabrillo-format-tutorial (read 2026-09-09) prints complete worked headers containing the literal lines "CONTEST: ARRL-SS-CW" and "CONTEST: ARRL-SS-SSB". So cabrillo_contest_token passes both through unchanged, and the crossing guard covers them. QSO-LINE COLUMN ORDER: the rules PDF publishes none ("ELOG.1. The official ARRL format for electronic logs is the Cabrillo format"), but the same arrl.org tutorial page publishes a QSO DATA TEMPLATE for Sweepstakes with a lettered legend — "E= Your call. F= Your QSO #. G= Your precedence. H= Your check … I= Your ARRL Section. J= The call of the station you worked. K= Their QSO number to you. L= Their precedence. M= Their check. N = Their ARRL Section." — over the sample line "QSO: 14000 CW 2009-11-07 2100 W1AW 1 M 38 CT K8MM 1 Q 92 MI". ⚠️ THE CALLSIGN IS THE STRUCTURAL COLUMN, FIRST OF EACH SIDE, AND THE EXCHANGE COLUMNS ARE SERIAL/PRECEDENCE/CHECK/SECTION WITH NO CALLSIGN AMONG THEM. The design sketch (§6.2) assumed the reverse and reserved the question for the batch that read the sponsor; the reading corrects it. PRECEDENCE: derived from the entry's declared category (contest_category_operator / _power / _assisted / _station), never typed, so the letter on every QSO line and the CATEGORY-* headers of the same entry are one fact; the power thresholds are the same PDF's Entry Categories table ("Version 1.6 – 20 Sep 2023"): QRP "5 watts PEP output or less", Low Power "100 watts PEP output or less", High Power "1500 watts PEP output or the maximum allowable power level established by the national licensing authority". An undeclared axis REFUSES the session with a sentence rather than defaulting — a default here is a category claim transmitted on every contact of a 24-hour contest. WINDOW: "Contest Period: Begins 2100 UTC Saturday and runs through 0259 UTC Monday" = start_hour_utc 21, duration_hours 30, month 11, nth_full weekend 1 (CW) and 3 (Phone). §1.1's 24-of-30-hour operating limit and §1.2's after-24-hours rule are NOT modelled: nothing in this build tracks off times, and a score that silently dropped contacts would be worse than one that does not know about the limit. UNESTABLISHED: whether ARRL's log robot validates the CONTEST token at all — the rules say only that electronic logs go to contest-log-submission.arrl.org, whose web form selects the contest.
_provenance.cqww_wpx: CQ WW DX and CQ WPX ship as FOUR rulesets — cqww_cw, cqww_ssb, cqwpx_cw, cqwpx_ssb — written from the sponsors' own current pages, all read 2026-09-09: https://www.cqww.com/rules/ ("The 2026 CQ World-Wide DX Contest"), https://cqwpx.com/rules/ ("2026 CQ World-Wide WPX Contest"), https://cqwpx.com/rules_faq.htm, https://cqww.com/cabrillo.htm and https://cqwpx.com/cabrillo.htm. FOUR AND NOT SIX: the team brief listed CQ-WW-RTTY and CQ-WPX-RTTY as further mode arms of these contests and they are NOT. Each sponsor's own cabrillo.htm says "The contest-name must be one of the following" over exactly TWO names, and ADIF 3.1.7's own labels name the other two as somebody else's contests — CQ-WW-RTTY = "CQ/RJ WW RTTY DX Contest" and CQ-WPX-RTTY = "CQ/RJ WW RTTY WPX Contest" (CQ/RJ = CQ + RTTY Journal), which have their own rules, their own exchanges (the RTTY events add a US state / Canadian province to the exchange and count it as a multiplier) and their own multiplier sets. Shipping either token on these rulesets would file a log under a contest whose rules it was not scored by. TWO RULESETS PER CONTEST rather than one mode-split row, for the reason Sweepstakes needed: a WindowRule holds ONE weekend and each mode is a different weekend. EXCHANGE. CQ WW (§III): "SSB: RS report plus CQ Zone number of the station transmitter location (e.g., 59 05). CW: RST report plus CQ Zone of the station transmitter location (e.g., 599 05)." — so the ZN slot is a Number 1..40 sourced from the contest_cq_zone setting, exported under ADIF's CQZ / MY_CQ_ZONE (both "PositiveInteger … in the range 1 to 40", adif.org/317, read 2026-09-09). CQ WPX (§IV): "RS(T) report plus a progressive contact serial number starting with 001 for the first contact." ⚠️ The same rule adds "Multi-Two, Multi-Unlimited, and Multi-Distributed entrants use separate serial number sequences on each band"; SerialScope::PerBand exists only to be REFUSED by name in this build, so these rulesets declare per_contest, which is right for every single-operator entry and wrong for those three multi categories. DUPE. CQ WW §IV.B "Stations may be contacted once on each band."; CQ WPX §V.B "A station may be worked once on each band for QSO point credit". by_call true, by_band true, by_mode_class FALSE — each ruleset is a single-mode weekend, so a mode axis inside one log has nothing to separate. POINTS — the first contest in this build priced by the RELATION between the two stations, not by mode class. CQ WW §IV.B: "Contacts between stations on different continents count three (3) points. Contacts between stations on the same continent but in different countries count one (1) point. Exception: Contacts between stations in different countries within the North American boundaries count two (2) points. Contacts between stations in the same country have zero (0) QSO point value, but count for zone and country multiplier credit." CQ WPX §V.B: "1. Contacts between stations on different continents are worth three (3) points on 28, 21, and 14 MHz and six (6) points on 7, 3.5, and 1.8 MHz. 2. Contacts between stations on the same continent, but different countries, are worth one (1) point on 28, 21, and 14 MHz and two (2) points on 7, 3.5, and 1.8 MHz. Exception: For North American stations only—contacts between stations within the North American boundaries (both stations must be located in North America) are worth two (2) points on 28, 21, and 14 MHz and four (4) points on 7, 3.5, and 1.8 MHz. 3. Contacts between stations in the same country are worth 1 point regardless of band." ⚠️ ARM 3 IS THE ONE THE DESIGN SPEC'S §14 WAS MISSING, and it is where the two contests diverge on the SAME relation: CQ WW gives a same-country contact ZERO and CQ WPX gives it ONE. That is exactly why relation_points is a table in this file and not a function in the code. The loader refuses a relation_points table that names no same_country, same_continent or different_continent row, because a missing arm scores those contacts at zero silently — which is the defect §14 had. MULTIPLIERS. CQ WW §IV.C: "There are two types of multipliers. Zone: A multiplier of one (1) for each different CQ Zone contacted on each band. The CQ Worked All Zones rules are the standard. Country: A multiplier of one (1) for each different country contacted on each band. The DXCC entity list, Worked All Europe (WAE) multiplier list plus IG9/IH9, and continental boundaries are the standards for defining country multipliers." — two INDEPENDENT per-band universes, one off the exchange (the zone) and one off the callsign (the entity), summed: "the sum of zone and country multipliers". CQ WPX §V.C: "Each PREFIX is counted only once regardless of the band or number of times the same prefix is worked." — per_log, off the callsign. THE PREFIX RULE. §V.C.1 verbatim: "A PREFIX is the letter/numeral combination which forms the first part of the amateur call. Examples: N8, W8, WD8, HG1, HG19, KC2, OE2, OE25, LY1000, etc. Any difference in the numbering, lettering, or order of same shall count as a separate prefix. In cases of portable operation, the portable designator will then become the prefix. The portable prefix must be an authorized prefix of the country/call area of operation. Portable designators without numbers will be assigned a zero (Ø) after the second letter of the portable designator to form the prefix. Example: PA/N8BJQ would become PAØ. All calls without numbers will be assigned a zero (Ø) after the first two letters to form the prefix. Example: XEFTJW would count as XEØ. Maritime mobile, mobile, /A, /E, /J, /P, or other license class identifiers do not count as prefixes." — plus the sponsor's own FAQ, which is where WHERE THE PREFIX ENDS is actually answered: "The prefix includes everything up to the end of the first numbers in the call. … OL25LP = OL25 / DL60CHILD = DL60 / 9A800VZ = 9A800 / DR2006Q = DR2006 / LY1000CW = LY1000 / KL7RA/WK9 = WK9 / OE/K5ZD = OEØ". ⚠️ "the first numbers" means the first digit run AFTER A LETTER, not the first digit: 9A800VZ is the sponsor's own counterexample (stopping at the leading 9 would give "9"), and 4U1ITU is the same shape and counts as 4U1. ⚠️ ONE ARM HAS NO SPONSOR WORKED EXAMPLE: a portable designator that is BARE DIGITS (W1AW/4). It is implemented as digit substitution on the base prefix (W1AW/4 = W4) from "the portable designator will then become the prefix" plus "must be an authorized prefix of the country/call area of operation" — a bare 4 is not an authorized prefix on its own. That reading is this build's, not the sponsor's. The whole rule is contest::callsign::wpx_prefix and every example above is a literal in its tests. CABRILLO. Tokens CQ-WW-CW / CQ-WW-SSB / CQ-WPX-CW / CQ-WPX-SSB, and for these four THE TWO REGISTRIES AGREE — verified separately, because a token confirmed in one says nothing about the other. ADIF 3.1.7's CONTEST_ID enumeration (https://adif.org/317/ADIF_317.htm, "updated 2026-03-22") carries all four; the WA7BNM master list (https://www.contestcalendar.com/cabnames.php, Revision Date February 23, 2026) carries the same four at ids 192, 172, 29 and 291; and both sponsors publish them directly with "Be sure to use hyphens as shown. DO NOT PUT THE YEAR OR USE PH INSTEAD OF SSB." So cabrillo_contest_token gets NO arm for any of them and the token test pins all four. QSO LINE: both sponsors publish the same template, "QSO: freq mo date time call rst exch call rst exch t", with samples "QSO: 3799 PH 2000-11-26 0711 N6TW 59 03 JT1Z 59 23 0" (CQ WW) and "QSO: 3799 PH 1999-03-06 0711 HC8N 59 001 W1AW 59 001 0" (CQ WPX) — which is §6.2's structural shape exactly. TRANSMITTER COLUMN: "Note for Column 81 (transmitter number): For the MULTI-ONE and MULTI-TWO categories, the last column in the log indicates which transmitter made the QSO. It must be a 0 or a 1. This column is not required for other categories." (WPX says the same for MULTI-TWO.) These four rulesets are the only ones that declare transmitter_column true; a single-position entry writes 0, which every sample line on both pages carries. ⚠️ A real MULTI-TWO entry's second transmitter must write 1 and this build has no second position to write it — the column is honest for one position and incomplete for two. WINDOWS. "SSB: October 24-25  CW: November 28-29 / Starts 00:00:00 UTC Saturday  Ends 23:59:59 UTC Sunday" (CQ WW) and "SSB: March 28-29  CW: May 30-31 / Starts: 0000 UTC Saturday Ends: 2359 UTC Sunday" (CQ WPX) — each the LAST FULL WEEKEND of its month, 0000Z Saturday, 48 hours. ⚠️ The WPX page prints "SSB: March 28-29, 2025" while its own log deadline says "SSB logs no later than 2359 UTC 31 March 2026": a sponsor typo in the year, and March 28-29 IS the last full weekend of March 2026. ⚠️ CQ WW's II and CQ WPX's III both restrict operation to six bands (1.8/3.5/7/14/21/28 MHz) and a ruleset has no band field, so that is not expressed; no score or dupe here depends on it, but a contact on 30 m would find no relation_points band row and score zero rather than being refused. ⚠️ CQ WPX's II ("Single Operator stations may operate 36 of the 48 hours") and CQ WW's off-time rules are not modelled — nothing in this build tracks off times, and a score that silently dropped contacts would be worse than one that does not know about the limit. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED. (1) "Maritime mobile stations count only for a zone multiplier" (CQ WW §IV.C). The country file places a /MM call by its home call, so a /MM contact counts a COUNTRY multiplier it should not — an over-count of one per distinct /MM entity worked, in a contest where a /MM contact is rare. The sponsor states no points rule for /MM at all, so the alternative (refusing to place a /MM call) would score its QSO points at zero, which is a bigger error in the other direction. (2) The MULTI-TWO transmitter id, above. (3) Overlay categories, off-time limits and the log-checking penalties, none of which a logger computes.
